summary: The 11 labels print GLA at 165 to 480 mg. Six name borage oil as the source (181851, 232718, 328569 as the row form; 223170, 218723, 77205 as a separate borage row), three carry it in a mixed omega blend that includes borage oil (304676, 327995, 332936), one prints safflower oil (65773) and one prints no source in an omega product (222789). For rheumatoid arthritis, Cochrane finds moderate evidence of some benefit from GLA oils (21328257), though the abstract states no doses. For eczema, oral borage and evening primrose oils lack effect (23633319). The one trial here with a named primary outcome and a label-range dose found 320 mg/day noninferior to alpha-lipoic acid on pain but not on total symptoms, with no placebo, in painful diabetic neuropathy (31701699), a purpose no label carries. Borage oil 1,000 mg lowered blood pressure against vitamin E (33534427). Borage oil at 880 mg GLA/day showed no effect on metabolic rate or BMI (34606560). Abstracts only. Reference only, no Evidence credit.
